title: Sounds like a strategy upgrade
text: Expansion kickoff skill, and it sounds like a strategy upgrade, like it studied business expansions and came back knowing something it didn't before.

title: Broken, with a case — delete the folder, nothing is forgotten
text: But nothing in the model changes. Delete the skills folder and Claude doesn't forget how to plan an expansion. There was nothing to learn. It just stops following that one routine.

title: The anchor: one file — expansion-kickoff's single SKILL.md
text: Here's what a skill actually is, one file. Expansion kickoff, for instance, is a folder holding a single skill. MD instructions for starting a structured checklist when a team or business expands somewhere new, written in plain language Claude reads before it starts.

title: Read it, then follow it in order
text: Claude reads that file top to bottom and works through it step-by-step in the order it's written, no branching unless the file itself says branch.

title: Spec, not power — the payoff and the limit
text: That makes a skill a specification, not a new power. The payoff, the same checklist every kickoff, the same starting steps every time. The limit, anything outside those written steps and Claude is off the map. So expansion

title: The anchor returns — same file, every run
text: Kickoff never taught Claude how to run a real expansion. It just guarantees that every time expansion kickoff runs, Claude reads that same file and starts the same structured checklist. That's the whole trick.

title: Both directions — neither one is proof
text: Watching Claude produce a tidy kickoff plan doesn't prove it understood the business. A file can be followed to the letter on a situation it never really grasped. title: Carry-out
text: Teach Claude how to run an expansion. It's a file of steps Claude reads before it starts. So every kickoff comes out with the same checklist every time.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Pick one process I repeat every time I start something new. Write me a skill. MD for it, plain language ordered steps, then read it back to me and walk me through exactly what you'll do before you do it.
